title: What If the Biggest Solar Storm Ever Hit Us Today?

scenes.text: What if the 1859 solar storm hit today? Back then, it set telegraph offices on fire.
Warning would range from a few minutes to about a day. After that, the particles arrive.
Long wires act like antennas, so power grids could trip all at once. GPS and phone signals could fail with them.
Satellite damage alone was once estimated at thirty to seventy billion dollars. Planes could be grounded without satellite guidance.
The first year could cost one to two trillion dollars. Full recovery might take four to ten years.
Storms this big come roughly once every five hundred years. Nobody can say when the next one is due.

description:
What if the 1859 Carrington solar storm hit today?
Grids, GPS and phones could fail together. The first year could cost $1 to $2 trillion, and recovery could take four to ten years.
What should we run through next?
